clue.text: Righteous extra farewell

parts.note: righteous means good, morally upright
a bye is an extra in cricket, a run scored without the bat touching the ball

explanation.surface: A pious person gives an extra-long goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both are parting words said on leaving someone.

clue.text: Cry when capturing leader of coup in German town

indicators.note: capturing means the town's name takes in and holds the next letter

parts.note: Gotha is a town in Thuringia, Germany

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the word coup

explanation.surface: A shout goes up when the head of a coup is seized in a German town.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal exclamation, 'got you', shouted when catching someone out.

clue.text: Hebrew patriarch losing head about awful one, a prophet

indicators.note: about means the shortened name goes around the other pieces
losing head means the patriarch's name drops its first letter

parts.note: Noah is a patriarch of the Hebrew Bible
awful means bad
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An Old Testament patriarch, beheaded for something awful, becomes a prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts NOAH to OAH, which goes 'about' BADIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Obadiah is the Hebrew prophet whose name heads the shortest book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Ships string bean I ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put in order, so these letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A shopper reports having ordered some string beans for the ship's galley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like buying, but here it means arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigantines are two-masted sailing vessels, each a kind of ship.

clue.text: A former ruler weary after uprising in African country

indicators.note: in a down answer, an uprising means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, refers to Queen Elizabeth
to weary is to tire

explanation.surface: A deposed ruler, tired out after a revolt in an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: AERTIRE is reversed; the letters ER are the late Queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a nation in the Horn of Africa, on the Red Sea coast.

clue.text: Copper's letters read aloud in farewell

indicators.note: says the two letters are spoken, giving the sound of two short words

parts.note: copper's chemical symbol is Cu, the two letters C and U

explanation.surface: A police officer's correspondence is read out at a leaving do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but here it is the metal, symbol Cu; said as letters, C-U.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual parting phrase, said when leaving someone you expect to meet again.

clue.text: Trimmed belly: about 45 inches!

indicators.note: trimmed means both ends are cut off the word belly

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a trimmed belly at a waistline of 45 inches.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes about a still-ample waist; the measure is an old cloth length.
explanation.definitionFit: An old English unit for cloth, equal to 45 inches.

clue.text: Covering gossip about two mums

indicators.note: about means the chatter word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to yak is to chatter, gossip
two senses of mum: SH, the call to keep mum, and MA, a mother
two senses of mum: SH, the call to keep mum, and MA, a mother

explanation.surface: Two mothers cover up while gossiping.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil worn by some Muslim women to cover the face in public.

clue.text: Finished and ruined, in conclusion

parts.note: time is up when it is finished
shot means ruined, worn out

explanation.surface: A project is finished and wrecked, as the final verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome or result of a process, its eventual conclusion.

clue.text: Complain as jeans are turned up without the slightest bit of needlework

indicators.note: without means outside, the jeans word going around the next piece
in a down answer, turned up means the brand's letters read upwards

parts.note: Levis are a brand of jeans

indicators.note: the slightest bit means just the first letter of the word needlework

explanation.surface: Someone moans that their jeans have been turned up without any stitching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: SIVEL goes round the N.
explanation.definitionFit: To snivel is to whine or moan tearfully, a weepy way to complain.

clue.text: AI distorts Latin translation — we like to do things the old way

definitions.text: we like to do things the old way

indicators.note: a translation turns words into new forms, so these letters are rendered in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An artificial intelligence garbles a Latin text, to the dismay of old-school scholars.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of AI DISTORTS LATIN gives the answer; 'distorts' is fodder, not the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservatives in custom and habit would say this of themselves: they prefer long-established ways.

clue.text: Some geisha I fancy in foreign port

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sailor admits to taking a liking to some geishas while docked abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Haifa is a major seaport in northern Israel, foreign from the setter's point of view.

clue.text: Slough House Joe getting one of the dogs switched on internally

indicators.note: the O in the middle of the dog's name is swapped out for the new letter

parts.note: Rover is a stock name for a pet dog, one of the canine kind
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A spy from the Slough House novels picks up a dog and switches it on.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough House is the MI5 dumping ground in Mick Herron's Slow Horses novels; 'Joe' is spy slang for an agent. 'one' gives I and also hints at a single dog, ROVER, whose inner O it replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: River Cartwright is the young agent at the heart of Mick Herron's spy series.

clue.text: Oleander obtained from nymph after party with Greek character

indicators.note: after means the nymph's name follows the party

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a do is a party
Daphne is the nymph of Greek myth who became a laurel

explanation.surface: A flowering shrub gets its name from a nymph, plus a party with a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhododaphne is an old name for oleander, the poisonous evergreen shrub.

clue.text: Low satellite that's waned

indicators.note: waned means shrunk, so the satellite's word loses its final letter

parts.note: the Moon is Earth's satellite

explanation.surface: A satellite drops low in the sky as it wanes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective about the satellite, but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To low is to make the sound of cattle, the same as the cow's call.

clue.text: Talks fall short unfortunately without resistance — there's no more

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
without means the letter for resistance is taken away from the word short

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Negotiations break down, sadly, because nobody would offer any resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes R from SHORT, leaving SHOT, which is jumbled with TALKS and FALL.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase that closes Looney Tunes cartoons, announcing the show is over.

clue.text: Attraction or repulsion of concert if game rearranged

indicators.note: rearranged plainly says these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Whether a gig appeals or repels may depend on a game being rescheduled.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet pulls unlike poles together and pushes like poles apart: that pull or push is the physics term.

clue.text: Ring-bearing girl the French found in ancient city

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the city's name

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
la is French for the

explanation.surface: A girl carrying a ring is discovered in an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Annular means ring-shaped, bearing or forming a ring, like an annular eclipse.

clue.text: Helmet that protects at the crease

indicators.note: protects means the word that wraps around and shields the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
in cricket a batter at the crease is in, batting

explanation.surface: A helmet protects a cricketer batting at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the line where a cricket batter stands; a batter there is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier's steel helmet, so called in slang.

clue.text: One fighting behind the lines cycling in ditch

indicators.note: cycling means letters are moved from one end of the words in ditch round to the other

explanation.surface: A soldier goes cycling and ends up in a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters, CH, go round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chindits were Allied special forces who fought deep behind Japanese lines in Burma in the Second World War.

clue.text: A letter from Greece opposing Italian import perhaps?

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means against, opposing

explanation.surface: A letter from Greece objects to Italian imports.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: one Italian import among many.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a Tuscan red wine, a typical import from Italy.

clue.text: Rock service provided

parts.note: Mass is a church service
provided means if, on condition that

explanation.surface: A rock service is laid on, a church event with guitars.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact mass of mountains, a great body of rock.

clue.text: State school's violent and sudden uprising

parts.note: to state is to put, express
SCH is the abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: A state school suffers a violent rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State school' reads as one thing; split it into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is an attempted coup, a sudden violent seizure of power.

clue.text: Darwin's regularly trimmed beard

indicators.note: regularly trimmed means every other letter is cut away, keeping the alternate ones

explanation.surface: Charles Darwin's famous beard was kept neatly trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: Darwin's beard is the picture, but the beard defined is that of a grass.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany the beard of barley or wheat is the bristly spike on each grain.

clue.text: Muslim in student body turned to the west

indicators.note: in an across answer, going west means reading from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
the NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: A Muslim in the student union turns towards the west.
explanation.walkthrough: Muslims turn east, towards Mecca, to pray from Britain; 'turned to the west' is the reversal signal for an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the larger of the two main branches of Islam.

clue.text: Farewell promotion Independent editor initially refused essentially

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

indicators.note: initially says the first letter of the word editor is taken
essentially points to the very centre, the middle letter of the word refused

explanation.surface: An advert is turned down by the Independent's editor, who says goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A French word for goodbye, used in English for a formal parting.

clue.text: Thus extensive genetic fingerprint reversal cheers in respect of complete school book

parts.note: thus means so
extensive means long

indicators.note: reversal says the genetic letters are read backwards

parts.note: DNA is used for genetic fingerprinting
cheers is British slang for thanks
for can mean concerning, in respect of
a school is a group of fish, so a complete school is every one of them

explanation.surface: A long-winded string of words thanks a school for its book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a place of learning but is a shoal of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth novel in Douglas Adams's Hitchhiker's Guide series is titled with this phrase.

clue.text: 12 reduced to 0

indicators.note: reduced means the Egyptian waterway's name is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: the answer to 12 across is a watercourse, and the Nile is an example

explanation.surface: Twelve cut down to zero.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference reads like a number; it points to the 12-across answer, defined by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is zero, especially as a sports score.
